units.passage: users are expected to employ AI technologies responsibly and to contribute to a culture of ethical AI practices. Ethical Use: AI technologies must be developed and used in ways that are consistent with ethical standards, human rights, and applicable laws. All users must employ AI technologies in an ethical manner that aligns with the University's code of conduct and values. Discriminatory, biased, malicious, or harmful use of AI is strictly prohibited. All AI development projects, applications or the use of AI driven automated decision making must undergo an ethical review by the data owner to assess their potential impact on individuals, communities, and society at large. Ethical use issues should be directed to the appropriate university office for review and resolution. Privacy and Data Protection: Personal data used in AI applications must be handled with the utmost care. Users must respect the privacy rights of individuals and handle personal, sensitive, and confidential data in accordance with relevant laws, regulations, and University policies. Intellectual Property: Users are expected to follow all UTRGV and UT System guidance and all applicable intellectual property and copyright laws, including respecting intellectual property rights related to AI technologies, including software, algorithms, models, and datasets.
units.why: Tells users to follow IP and copyright law for AI technologies (software, models, datasets); P52 covers copyright and ownership.

units.why: Users "should assume that AI-generated text, images, and code may not be eligible for copyright protection or may inadvertently infringe"; copyright of AI output, P52.

units.passage: users should consult the University’s Intellectual Property Policy and Copyright Infringement and Illegal File Sharing Policy before incorporating AI-generated materials into their work.
units.policy: Users consult the University's Intellectual Property Policy and Copyright Infringement and Illegal File Sharing Policy before incorporating AI-generated materials into their work.
units.why: Users "should consult the University's Intellectual Property Policy and Copyright Infringement and Illegal File Sharing Policy before incorporating AI-generated materials into their work"; this directs them to copyright and IP rules for AI output, so P52, should.
units.fit_note: Directs users to other university policies before using AI-generated material.

units.passage: Currently, ownership of content generated by Gen AI remains unresolved at the federal level, and there is no clear standard regarding its ownership .
units.why: "ownership of content generated by Gen AI remains unresolved at the federal level" states a fact about IP ownership of AI output, so P52 informs.

units.passage: It is prohibited to upload or use content that is copyrighted or infringes on the rights of any third party.
units.why: "It is prohibited to upload or use content that is copyrighted or infringes on the rights of any third party" bans copyrighted inputs, so P52 (copyright) with a fit note since it is a prohibition.
units.fit_note: A direct ban on uploading copyrighted content, not just a consideration of licensing.

units.passage: Be mindful of any rights the platform may claim over the content you create using their system.
units.why: "Be mindful of any rights the platform may claim over the content you create using their system" raises ownership and licensing, so P52.

units.passage: The Policy on Intellectual Property (Policy 13000) would benefit from clarification of ownership frameworks for AI-generated works (see Appendix B: Research Domain findings, Section B.2.3) and collaboration agreements that address the complex intersection of human creativity and artificial intelligence capabilities. This revision must systematically address patent and copyright implications for AI-assisted research while protecting both institutional and individual researcher interests.
units.why: The IP policy needs 'clarification of ownership frameworks for AI-generated works' (P52).

units.passage: The university should leverage external resources (legal advice) in order to work with the campus community to develop best practices around copyright related to AI- generated content, including but not limited to citation, attribution, authorship, and research innovation
units.why: 'The university should leverage external resources (legal advice) ... to develop best practices around copyright related to AI-generated content' is a copyright task, P52.

units.passage: The following recommendations apply: • W&M should support individuals so that they can comply with the relevant copyright rules and norms. o The university should leverage external resources (legal advice) in order to work with the campus community to develop best practices around copyright related to AI- generated content, including but not limited to citation, attribution, authorship, and research innovation. • GenAI users should adhere to state, local, and federal laws around copyright, especially those laws around fair use. • GenAI users should adhere to the university’s code of conduct around academic integrity, plagiarism and the use of unauthorized resources. • GenAI users should remain apprised of current developments in GenAI copyright law, because copyright law focusing on GenAI continues to be a developing topic. • GenAI users should not input university or personal intellectual property into non-approved GenAI applications.
units.why: 'GenAI users should adhere to state, local, and federal laws around copyright, especially those laws around fair use' (P52); all, general, should.
units.fit_note: Concerns copyright and fair use specifically (also P52).

units.passage: Regent Policy 25-3 prohibits the use of System IT resources to perpetrate harassment or stalking or to violate laws or policies. You may not use AI tools or services to infringe copyright or other intellectual property rights.
units.policy: You may not use AI tools or services to infringe copyright or other intellectual property rights.
units.why: 'You may not use AI tools or services to infringe copyright or other intellectual property rights' is a copyright rule (P52).

units.passage: Entering copyrighted material into a generative AI tool or service may effectively result in the creation of a digital copy, which is a copyright violation
units.why: 'Entering copyrighted material ... may effectively result in the creation of a digital copy' explains the copyright risk (P52).

units.passage: In addition, entering research results into a generative AI tool or service could constitute premature disclosure, compromising invention patentability
units.policy: In addition, entering research results into a generative AI tool or service could constitute premature disclosure, compromising invention patentability.
units.why: 'entering research results into a generative AI tool or service could constitute premature disclosure, compromising invention patentability' is a research IP risk (P52).

units.passage: In addition to violating UW policies, many of the above uses also violate generative AI providers’ policies and terms
units.policy: In addition to violating UW policies, many of the above uses also violate generative AI providers’ policies and terms.
units.why: 'many of the above uses also violate generative AI providers’ policies and terms' notes provider terms of use (P52).
units.fit_note: Provider terms, not copyright or ownership as such.
